content.title: About
content.content: Pasteurized whole raw eggs that are flash‑frozen retain all nutrients and safety. Freezing allows long‑term storage without quality loss.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pasteurization destroys most pathogenic bacteria, including Salmonella.
Frozen eggs are widely used in industrial baking and confectionery.
An egg is about 60 % protein and 30 % fat, the rest being water and minerals.
Raw eggs can be stored frozen for up to 12 months without flavor deterioration.
Pasteurized eggs are safer for recipes that do not involve heat treatment.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Egg white provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Eggs are one of the few natural food sources of vitamin D, supporting bone health and immunity.

items.title: Contains choline
items.content: Choline is important for liver function, brain development, and fat metabolism.

items.title: Provides vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell formation and nervous system health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Eggs contain virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk if mishandled
items.content: Improper thawing can allow bacterial growth.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: A large egg contains about 186 mg of cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol should monitor intake.

items.title: Not recommended for infants under 1 year
items.content: Raw eggs can be hard to digest and pose a bacterial risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thawed eggs can be used in baking, omelets, sauces, custards, and desserts. They are convenient for adding to batters without cracking fresh eggs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen eggs at –18 °C in an airtight package. Thaw in the refrigerator for 12–24 hours. Do not thaw at room temperature. Use thawed eggs within 2–3 days.
